sources.title: Study finds giraffes may be capable of rudimentary math - UPI
Giraffes combine quantities similarly to addition - University of Barcelona
Giraffes combine quantities similarly to addition - Phys.org

chunks.text: Scientists have {{found out}} that giraffes can do simple math. Researchers at the University of Barcelona {{carried out}} a study with four giraffes at a zoo in Spain. They wanted to see whether the animals could {{work out}} which [[amount]] of food was bigger. The results surprised many people.

verbs.wrong: To prove something that people already believed
To pay for and support a piece of research
verbs.correct: To do or perform a task

verbs.wrong: To notice something quickly without thinking
verbs.correct: To find the answer to something

chunks.text: In the test, the scientists {{set up}} clear [[containers]] with different numbers of carrot and vegetable pieces. Sometimes they added more pieces, and sometimes they {{took away}} a few. Each time, the giraffes had to {{pick out}} the container with more food. To get the [[reward]], the animals used their long tongues to reach it.

verbs.wrong: To hide something so it cannot be seen easily
To count how many things are left
To point at something you want
verbs.correct: To choose one thing from several

chunks.text: When the scientists added pieces, the giraffes did far better than luck alone would explain. According to the study, they chose the larger amount about 68 percent of the time. This helped the team {{rule out}} the idea that the animals were only guessing. The results suggest giraffes can {{keep track of}} small numbers and can {{tell apart}} large and small amounts of food. However, the animals could not solve harder tasks, such as subtraction.

verbs.wrong: To show that an idea is only partly true
verbs.correct: To decide that something is not possible

verbs.wrong: To compare two numbers to see which is bigger
verbs.correct: To follow the number or progress of something

verbs.wrong: To choose the thing that you like best
verbs.correct: To see the difference between things

chunks.text: For a long time, people thought that only humans and a few [[clever]] animals, such as [[primates]] and [[crows]], had a sense of numbers. This new study adds to a growing list of animals that can count in some way. The researchers now want to {{carry on}} their work with other zoo animals. They hope it will help us {{figure out}} more about how animal minds work.

To watch something very closely for a long time

tf.s: Researchers carried on a new study with four giraffes at a zoo in Spain.
tf.why: The researchers carried out (performed) a new study. Carry on means to continue something that is already happening.

tf.s: In the test, the giraffes had to pick out the container that held more food.
tf.why: Each time, the giraffes had to pick out (choose) the container with more food to get the reward.

tf.s: Sometimes the scientists picked out a few pieces of food from the containers.
tf.why: Sometimes the scientists took away (removed) a few pieces. Pick out means to choose one thing from several, not to remove one.

tf.s: Scientists found out that giraffes can do simple math.
tf.why: Researchers at the University of Barcelona found out (discovered) that giraffes can do simple math.

tf.s: The researchers want to carry on their work with other zoo animals.
tf.why: The team wants to carry on (continue) their research to learn more about how animal minds work.

tf.s: This new study takes away from the growing list of animals that can count in some way.
tf.why: The study adds to (makes bigger) the growing list of animals that can count. Take away from means to make smaller, the opposite.
